title: Government Documents Accessible on NAS Archives Online
what_it_is: Government Documents Accessible on NAS Archives Online

sections.label: National Archives Government records access
sections.summary: NAS holds about two million public archives over 25 years old, with 160,000 records' metadata publicly accessible online and more to be declassified.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Currently, the National Archives of Singapore (NAS) has about two million Government records in its custody that are more than 25 years old and are deemed as public archives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Not all Government records can be released for open access, especially those that relate to our national defence, foreign relations and internal security, as well as documents which may be bound by confidentiality obligations or personal privacy reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: At present, the metadata of 160,000 records are publicly accessible on the NAS Archives Online portal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: This number will grow as we work with Government agencies to progressively declassify Government records.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: All declassified records are publicly searchable on the Online portal.

sections.label: Officers sent for declassification training
sections.summary: 750 officers from Government agencies were sent for basic declassification training in recent years to help them declassify well and quicker.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In fact, we have, in recent years, sent 750 officers from different Government agencies for basic declassification training in the hope that this will help more officers understand the importance of declassification, and to do it well and to do it quicker.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In terms of definition of researchers, this is based on our common understanding of what they do.

sections.label: Public requests for NAS information
sections.summary: Not all documents are freely available on NAS Online, but the public can request information and NAS staff will facilitate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Not all the documents are actually made freely available on the NAS Online – there are 160,000 or so – without conditions to everyone who just wants to access it online.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Also, to add on to my reply to the Member's earlier question, Members of the public can also make requests for this information and our NAS staff will also facilitate.
